name: natyv Markup
comment: Deliberately minimal (~/.claude/plans/lexical-wishing-penguin.md, Stage 3): comments and expose/uses keywords only, delegating everything else to source.go. An earlier, more ambitious version of this file tried to also highlight tags/attributes here directly -- confirmed via a real offline vscode-textmate/vscode-oniguruma test harness that VS Code's own bundled Go grammar wins same-position ties against a locally-declared rule regardless of declared order, so tag/attribute/string/expression highlighting is handled by the server's own real textDocument/semanticTokens/full instead, which has the real parse tree and doesn't need to guess. The one exception is the 'childText' injection below: a widget's own child text (e.g. Save in <Button>Save</Button>) has no real Go token of its own to be, so leaving it to source.go means it gets colored as a bare identifier (variable.other.go) purely by coincidence -- semantic tokens can't override that, since an *absent* semantic token falls back to whatever the base grammar already produced, it doesn't fall back to the editor's plain default foreground. The injection intercepts that specific span before source.go's own patterns see it, so it gets no scope at all -- confirmed via the same offline harness both that it fixes the reported case and its one real, accepted false positive (a same-line double-comparison with no intervening braces, e.g. '(x > 5) == (y < 10)', loses coloring for the middle fragment -- rare in practice, and composer bodies are pure markup with no interleaved plain comparisons anyway; logic-file code outside composer bodies is the only place this could ever fire).

patterns.comment: The <%...%> raw-code escape's own sentinel (2026-09-02). First attempt at this put these two rules in the top-level `patterns` array instead of here -- confirmed broken via a real 'Developer: Inspect Editor Tokens and Scopes' check in a live Extension Development Host: both '<' and '%' still resolved to plain source.go operator scopes with no ntx scope anywhere in the stack, i.e. exactly the same same-position-tie loss against VS Code's bundled Go grammar this file's own top comment already documents for any top-level rule. Only works as an injection, same as childText below.
patterns.name: punctuation.section.embedded.begin.ntx

patterns.comment: A run of plain text strictly between a '>' and the next '<' -- a widget's own child text (<Label>this part</Label>). Excludes '{'/'}' so it never crosses into a real Go block, which is what keeps this from swallowing ordinary multi-line Go code that happens to contain both comparison operators. Re-checked against the <%...%> raw-code escape (2026-09-02, editor-support pass for ~/.claude/plans/lexical-wishing-penguin.md's Phase B1) via the same real offline harness: a nested tag's own child text (e.g. Save in <% for _, m := range xs { <Button>Save</Button> } %>) still gets correctly blanked, and the realistic authoring pattern of putting a comparison directly in a tag's own attribute (<Badge tone={count > 0} />) is untouched, since '{'/'}' already protects it. The one real false positive this re-check found is a narrower instance of the class already accepted above: a bare, semicolon-joined statement sharing a line with a following tag and no intervening brace (e.g. 'x := count > 0; <Badge tone={x} />') loses coloring on the trailing fragment between the comparison and the tag -- same 'rare in practice' reasoning as above (idiomatic Go doesn't join statements with semicolons on one line, and the natural way to use a derived boolean is directly inside the tag's own {} attribute, which is safe). Accepted rather than fixed: a real fix needs actual tag-boundary tracking, which is exactly the complexity this file's own top-level comment already explains was rejected in favor of the LSP's real semantic tokens.
